grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is whole food: potatoes, chard, eggs, crème fraîche, smoked haddock and salad leaves.

supermarket.reason: Tesco sells every ingredient, and 250g of smoked haddock is an everyday purchase.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a saucepan, an ovenproof frying pan and a whisk, and starting on the hob before finishing in the oven is within a beginner's reach.

works.reason: Eight eggs with potatoes, chard and haddock make a generous frittata for four, and raw haddock chunks will cook through in 18 minutes of hob and oven time.

honest_times.reason: Halving potatoes, slicing onions and chard, cutting the fish and whisking fit in 20 minutes, and the cook time roughly matches the 12-minute boil, softening and 15-minute bake.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, dill included, is used in the steps, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A frittata with salad suits an early June lunch, and 250g of chard, stalks and leaves, is a central part of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, plain British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a proper meal of eggs, fish, potatoes and greens served with salad.
